```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

scipR writes a [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip) index for an R
project: every definition and reference in the sources, with stable symbol
IDs, serialized as protobuf. Code search and navigation tools read that file
to answer "where is this defined" and "who calls this" without re-parsing R.

Most users run scipR as a command, `scip-r`, from a shell, a Makefile or a CI
job. This vignette sets that command up, shows how to index the common kinds
of R project, and then does the same from R and reads the result back.

## Setting up the `scip-r` command

scipR builds its command line with [Rapp](https://github.com/r-lib/Rapp).
Rapp comes from CRAN as a dependency. Install scipR, then the launcher:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("phisanti/scip-R")

scipR::install_scip_cli()
```

`install_scip_cli()` writes a small `scip-r` script into Rapp's bin
directory: `~/.local/bin` on macOS and Linux, and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\R\Rapp\bin` on Windows. Set `RAPP_BIN_DIR` before
calling it to choose another directory, or pass one directly:

```r
scipR::install_scip_cli(destdir = "~/bin")
```

That directory must be on your `PATH`. On macOS or Linux, if the shell
cannot find `scip-r`, add this to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

Check the installation:

```bash
scip-r --version
scip-r --help
```

The launcher records the absolute paths of `Rscript` and of the installed
package. Run `scipR::install_scip_cli()` again after upgrading R or moving
scipR to another library. Loading or updating the package never touches an
existing launcher.

## Indexing from the command line

Run `scip-r` with the project root, an output file and the files to index:

```bash
scip-r --root path/to/project --output index.scip --include "R/**/*.R"
```

`--root` defaults to the current directory and `--output` to `index.scip`,
so inside the project this is enough:

```bash
cd path/to/project
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R"
```

### Choosing files with `--include`

`--include` takes a glob relative to the root and can be repeated. `**`
matches any number of directories, including none, so `"R/**/*.R"` matches
both `R/utils.R` and `R/models/fit.R`. Quote the patterns so the shell does
not expand them.

Without `--include`, scip-r indexes every R file not excluded by
`.gitignore`, `.Rbuildignore` or its built-in list of generated directories.
For a real project, always pass `--include`: a project using renv keeps a
copy of every dependency's source under `renv/`, and indexing those takes
far longer and fills the index with other packages' symbols.

Patterns for common layouts:

```bash
# A package
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R"

# A package with scripts under inst/ and its tests
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R" --include "inst/**/*.R" --include "tests/**/*.R"

# A Shiny app or analysis project without a package layout
scip-r --include "app/**/*.R" --include "modules/**/*.R" --include "scripts/**/*.R"

# Lowercase .r files too
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R" --include "R/**/*.r"
```

The first progress line says how many files matched:

```
ℹ Phase 1: Parsing 412 files...
```

If no file matches, scip-r stops with an error naming the patterns and
writes no index; a `--root` that does not exist fails the same way. Both exit
with a non-zero status, so a Makefile or CI job stops there.

### Other options

```bash
# Resolve symbols with 4 parallel workers (worth it from about 50 files)
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R" --parallel 4

# Cache file hashes under .scip-r/ between runs
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R" --cache

# Set the project name used in symbol IDs (defaults to the root directory name)
scip-r --include "R/**/*.R" --project-name myproject
```

If parallel workers cannot start, for example in a sandbox that blocks local
sockets, scip-r falls back to sequential indexing and still writes the full
index.

The project name is part of every global symbol ID
(`scip-r r myproject 0.1.0 clean_scores().`). By default it is the name of the
root directory, so the same project cloned into a differently named folder gets
different IDs. Set `--project-name` explicitly in CI and anywhere else the
checkout path varies.

Both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` work. Pass `--help` for the full list.

### In a Makefile or CI job

The index is a build artifact. Regenerate it from a committed tree and keep
it out of version control:

```make
index.scip: $(shell find R -name '*.R')
	scip-r --root . --output $@ --include "R/**/*.R"
```

```bash
echo "*.scip" >> .gitignore
```

Code intelligence tools that read SCIP take the file as input, for example
Sourcegraph's `src code-intel upload -file=index.scip`.

## Indexing from R

The rest of this vignette builds a small package, indexes it from R with
`index_project()`, and reads the index back to show what it contains.

### A small project

The project has two files. `summarise_scores()` in `R/report.R` calls
`clean_scores()` from `R/clean.R`, and `print.score_report()` is an S3 method.

```{r project}
root <- file.path(tempdir(), "scorepkg")
dir.create(file.path(root, "R"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

writeLines(c(
  "Package: scorepkg",
  "Version: 0.1.0",
  "Title: Example Scores",
  "Description: A tiny package to index.",
  "License: MIT"
), file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION"))

writeLines(c(
  "clean_scores <- function(x) {",
  "  x[!is.na(x)]",
  "}"
), file.path(root, "R", "clean.R"))

writeLines(c(
  "summarise_scores <- function(x) {",
  "  kept <- clean_scores(x)",
  "  structure(list(mean = mean(kept), n = length(kept)), class = \"score_report\")",
  "}",
  "",
  "print.score_report <- function(x, ...) {",
  "  cat(\"mean:\", x$mean, \"over\", x$n, \"scores\\n\")",
  "  invisible(x)",
  "}"
), file.path(root, "R", "report.R"))
```

### Building the index

`index_project()` takes the same settings as the `scip-r` command line.
`include` limits indexing to the given globs. Always set it for real
projects, so dependency folders such as `renv/` are not walked.

```{r index, message = FALSE}
library(scipR)

output <- file.path(tempdir(), "scorepkg.scip")
index_project(list(
  root = root,
  output = output,
  include = "R/**/*.R",
  cache = FALSE,
  parallel = 0L,
  `project-name` = NULL
))

file.exists(output)
```

This is the same run as `scip-r --root scorepkg --output scorepkg.scip
--include "R/**/*.R"`.

### Reading the index

The schema ships with the package, so any protobuf reader can open the
file. With RProtoBuf:

```{r read}
proto <- system.file("scip.proto", package = "scipR")
if (!tryCatch(is.object(RProtoBuf::P("scip.Index")), error = function(e) FALSE)) {
  RProtoBuf::readProtoFiles(proto)
}
index <- RProtoBuf::read(RProtoBuf::P("scip.Index"), output)

vapply(as.list(index$documents), function(doc) doc$relative_path, character(1))
```

Each document lists the symbols it defines:

```{r symbols}
report <- Filter(
  function(doc) doc$relative_path == "R/report.R",
  as.list(index$documents)
)[[1]]

data.frame(
  name = vapply(as.list(report$symbols), function(s) s$display_name, character(1)),
  symbol = vapply(as.list(report$symbols), function(s) s$symbol, character(1))
)
```

### Following a call across files

An occurrence ties a source range to a symbol. The call to `clean_scores()`
in `R/report.R` carries the same symbol ID as its definition in `R/clean.R`;
that shared ID is what lets a tool jump from the call to the definition.

```{r occurrences}
occurrence_table <- function(doc) {
  occs <- as.list(doc$occurrences)
  data.frame(
    file = doc$relative_path,
    line = vapply(occs, function(o) o$range[1] + 1L, numeric(1)),
    symbol = vapply(occs, function(o) o$symbol, character(1)),
    definition = vapply(occs, function(o) bitwAnd(o$symbol_roles, 1L) == 1L, logical(1))
  )
}

occs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(as.list(index$documents), occurrence_table))
calls <- occs[endsWith(occs$symbol, " clean_scores()."), ]
rownames(calls) <- NULL
calls
```

SCIP ranges are 0-based; the table adds 1 to show editor line numbers.

## Options reference

Each `index_project()` field matches a command-line flag.


| Field | CLI flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `root` | `--root` | Project directory to index. |
| `output` | `--output` | Destination `.scip` file. |
| `include` | `--include` | Globs to index (repeatable). `NULL` indexes every non-ignored R file. |
| `cache` | `--cache` | Store file hashes under `.scip-r/state.rds`. |
| `parallel` | `--parallel` | Number of `mirai` workers; `0` is sequential. |
| `project-name` | `--project-name` | Project name used in global symbol IDs and metadata; defaults to the name of the root directory. |
